sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Starting the app
sections.what: Starts the app: finds the empty root element on the page, places the whole application inside it, and loads the global styles.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is the standard way a React app is started, and the strict wrapper helps catch mistakes early.
sections.watch_out: The app crashes at startup if the root element is missing from the HTML page.

summary: The entry point that starts the React app by placing it into the page's empty root element and loading the global styles.
purpose: Runs the app when the page opens.
why: Standard way a React app starts. The strict mode wrapper flags common mistakes during development.
how: It finds the page element named root, then renders the main App component inside a strict mode wrapper. It also loads the global stylesheet.
inputs: The page element named root from index.html, the App component, and the stylesheet.
outputs: The rendered app on the page.
risks: If the root element is missing, the app crashes at startup because the code assumes it exists.
debug: If the page is blank, check that index.html has an element named root and that the script path is correct. Check the browser console for the first error.
